document: bp vetting & clearance web pages (vessel clearance, management of change, structural assurance)
applies_to: Third-party vessels interacting with any bp asset
age_limits: Oil/chemical tankers >5,000 dwt: max 20 years. <5,000 dwt and LPG carriers: 25 years. LNG carriers: 40 years. Combination carriers >15 years not approved.
sire_report_age: Current operational SIRE report less than 6 months old (unless otherwise notified). Newbuilds: operational SIRE within 3 months of delivery (NBQ process may be used until then).
cap_rules: Oil, chemical & LPG tankers >20,000 dwt: minimum CAP 2 after reaching 15 years or by end of 3rd special survey, whichever is sooner. LNG >20 years: CAP 2 by 4th special survey or 20 years, whichever earlier. CAP 2 valid max 3 years from last day of survey.
other_criteria: Screened against latest bp SIRE plus owner profile, terminal feedback, casualty data, PSC. Owner/manager assessed via bp company assessment (TMSA-based). IGS, if fitted, must be operational and in use. Hydrostatic balanced loading not approved.
verify_note: Summary only. Criteria change and may be applied case by case; always verify at source before relying on it.
flags: Inconsistency on bp's own pages: the vetting-and-clearance index page says CAP 2 'after reaching 20 years of age or by fourth special survey', while the structural assurance page says 15 years / 3rd special survey for tankers >20,000 dwt. Check with bp.

document: ADNOC Ship Vetting Standards, s.9 and s.11, plus Vetting FAQs (web)
applies_to: Vessels nominated to ADNOC / ADNOC Group business
age_limits: Oil & chemical: >5,000 DWT 20 years, <5,000 DWT 25 years. LPG 25. LNG 40. Combination carriers 15. Ocean-going tanker barges 25. Inland tanker barges 30. Age from IOPP delivery date.
sire_report_age: Latest SIRE completed within last 6 months, plus at least one ADNOC SIRE report within the previous 24 months. A fresh SIRE may be required after a PSC detention or an incident in the last 12 months. Idle-status inspection: one-off acceptance valid 3 months. SIRE-BIQ (barges): 12 months (ocean-going tanker barges 6 months).
cap_rules: Oil, chemical or LPG carriers >15 years and >20,000 DWT: CAP 2 hull-structure certificate valid 5 years. LNG >20 years: CAP 2 hull, valid 5 years.
other_criteria: Double hull only for oil. TMSA updated within 12 months, minimum stage 2 in every element. Crew matrix aggregates (Master+C/O): 2 yrs with operator, 3 yrs in rank, 4 yrs on type, 8 yrs on all tankers. English 'Good' minimum. PSC deficiencies/detentions in last 12 months assessed. Only SIRE reports downloaded directly from OCIMF are used.
verify_note: Summary only. Criteria change and may be applied case by case; always verify at source before relying on it.

document: Oil, Gas and Chemical Vessel Vetting Baseline Criteria, Revision 4.0
applies_to: Tankers, LPG, LNG vetted by RightShip; recommended minimum baseline that customers can tailor
age_limits: Max 25 years tankers, 25 years LPG, 35 years LNG. Case-by-case exceptions for specific trading areas (e.g. Great Lakes).
sire_report_age: Acceptable SIRE / CDI physical examination within the previous 6 months. Unacceptable last SIRE/CDI = unacceptable until a new acceptable inspection.
cap_rules: Tanker or LPG >20,000 DWT and 15 years or over; any LNG >20 years: CAP 2 minimum for hull structure, machinery and cargo systems, issued by an IACS member, with Level 2 FDA (simplified fatigue design analysis) or equivalent; max validity 36 months from last date of survey.
other_criteria: 3+ PSC detentions in 24 months = Unacceptable; 2 in 24 months or 1 in 12 months = subject to review. Crew matrix dated within past 30 days (Annex 1 matrix). HVPQ not updated in last 3 months = subject to review. Non-IACS class, no IG P&I, PSC-banned vessel, or Very High Risk Paris/Tokyo MoU flag = Unacceptable.
verify_note: Summary only. Criteria change and may be applied case by case; always verify at source before relying on it.
flags: Baseline only: each RightShip vetting customer can set stricter rules.

document: Repsol Vetting – Marine Assurance Process & Safety Criteria (T&T-PROC-001/2020)
applies_to: SIRE vessels (tankers, barges, tugs) and bulk carriers proposed for Repsol use
age_limits: Tankers (crude/oil/bitumen/chemical) 25 years. LPG 30. LNG 40. OBO/OO/combination 15. Bunker barge 25. Barge 30. Tug/towboat 40. Age from initial delivery date.
sire_report_age: <20 years: Repsol safety inspection or OCIMF inspection no older than 6 months, or Repsol physical inspection no older than 12 months. ≥20 years: OCIMF inspection ≤6 months AND Repsol physical ≤6 months or Repsol safety inspection ≤3 months. BIRE vessels: OCIMF report ≤12 months.
cap_rules: Vessels ≥15 years and >5,000 MT SDWT: at least CAP 2 (GOOD) for hull, machinery and cargo handling from the 15th anniversary of delivery; certificates valid 3 years. <5,000 MT SDWT ≥15 years: thickness measurements reviewed.
other_criteria: Non-full-IACS class rejected. Owners must keep IG P&I entry (non-IG reviewed case by case). No pre-approval: each nomination screened.
verify_note: Summary only. Criteria change and may be applied case by case; always verify at source before relying on it.

applies_to: Vessels for Cepsa/Moeve charters, COAs and Cepsa terminals
age_limits: >25 years not suitable. >20 years and >40,000 MT SDWT not suitable. Tankers >15 years not suitable for a new time charter (extensions case by case). >15 years not suitable for COA, exceptionally up to 18 years with CAP 1 and Cepsa physical inspection. OBO >15 years not suitable.
sire_report_age: 15–19 years: if not already inspected by Cepsa and within re-inspection period, may exceptionally be suitable with a SIRE inspection within the last six months.
cap_rules: Crude tankers and product carriers >15 years and >20,000 DWT: minimum CAP 2 for hull, machinery and cargo systems. All vessels >20 years: CAP 2. >15,000 DWT, >15 years, carrying heavy fuel oil: CAP 1 plus Cepsa physical inspection and no PSC detentions with present technical managers in last 5 years. CAP only from IACS members; max validity 3 years.
other_criteria: 20–24 years: must be inspected by Cepsa (or within re-inspection period) before fixing. Officer matrix recommendation (combined senior officers): 2 yrs with operator, 3 yrs in rank, 6 yrs on type. IACS class only.
verify_note: Summary only. Criteria change and may be applied case by case; always verify at source before relying on it.
flags: Document dated December 2018 and still Cepsa-branded; may be superseded. Two-column PDF layout, read carefully at source.

age_limits: Oil & chemical tankers <5,000 DWT: max 25 years. >5,000 DWT: max 22 years (document text reads '22 (twenty)'). LPG: max 22. OBO/OO: max 20. Based on delivery date.
sire_report_age: SIRE/CDI carried out no later than 6 months before end of intended operation. Oil/chem >5,000 DWT aged 20–22: SIRE/CDI no more than 4 months before intended operation.

document: Marine Environmental, Safety and Quality Assurance Criteria – International ocean/seagoing tankers, 2017 edition
sire_report_age: Only valid OCIMF (SIRE) or CDI reports evaluated. 'Strongly Preferred' that SIRE/CDI reports are no more than six months old.
cap_rules: >15 years and >5,000 DWT: Hull CAP grade 1 or 2 (IACS society). All tankers >15 years: CAP for machinery & cargo systems grade 1 or 2. CAP renewed every 5 years; if older than 20 years, every 30 months.
other_criteria: Tankers >15 years must submit last special survey documentation (ESP file, thickness measurements, CAP fatigue assessment, coating reports, class status) for review.

applies_to: Vessels proposed to load at Westridge / Burnaby
age_limits: Tankers should be <15 years; up to and including 20 years may be acceptable with CAP 2 or better for both CAP Hull and CAP MC. Tugs and barges <30 years (waivable case by case).
sire_report_age: Recorded in the SIRE or OVID database within the preceding 7 months (12 months for tugs attending barges).
cap_rules: 15–20 years: CAP rating level 2 or better for CAP Hull and CAP MC; CAP certificates required for tankers over 15 years.
other_criteria: Flag not on latest Paris MoU blacklist (greylist needs special dispensation). Acceptable class; IG P&I meeting CLC/Bunkers 'Blue Card' cover; certified SMS; no OBO/combination carriers; not under a Trans Mountain technical hold.
verify_note: Summary only. Criteria change and may be applied case by case; always verify at source before relying on it.
